minutes.headline: Design committee debates elevator/annex options for Town Hall-Ritter renovation; no vote taken.
minutes.summary: The Building Design Committee reviewed member impressions from touring Town Hall and Ritter, discussed the Taylor & Burns floor plans, and spent most of the meeting debating where to place a new elevator and whether to rebuild the 1965 Ritter annex to resolve the buildings' split-level access problem. One member raised abandoning Ritter for a new or purchased building, but others pushed back strongly on cost and the symbolic value of keeping town government downtown; no formal decision was reached on layout, and the committee agreed to keep exploring options before its next meeting on November 17th.

what_happened.line: The committee will not bring a firm layout to November town meeting, only a status update, aiming for real options by May.
Members debated where to put a new elevator and whether to rebuild the 1965 Ritter annex to fix the two buildings' split-level access, reaching no decision.
One member raised abandoning Ritter for a new or purchased building; others pushed back on cost and on moving town government out of downtown.
The committee set aside the Brooks House as outside its scope and suggested a separate committee study non-town uses for it and 925 Mass. Ave.
Chris Ruth will work with the town manager on a bubble-diagram layout of which offices should sit together; next meeting is November 17th.

why_it_matters: This shapes a Town Hall/Ritter renovation residents will eventually vote to fund at town meeting, and the committee is explicitly delaying that ask until May.
Whether the town keeps offices downtown or builds/buys new touches both the tax bill and where residents go for town services.
The Brooks House and 925 Mass. Ave. being punted to a possible new committee means their future use remains undecided for now.
